analysis.one_liner: NTPC is India's largest power generator, a government-owned utility running coal-fired thermal plants plus a fast-growing renewable arm (NTPC Green Energy), selling power to state distribution companies under regulated, cost-plus tariffs.
analysis.whats_happening: The stock closed at ₹313.35, just above its 52-week low of ₹309.70 and 25.6% below the September 2024 peak of ₹421.29. Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) results showed standalone PAT up 11.9% YoY to ₹5,342 crore on revenue up 3%, and consolidated PAT up 12.9% to ₹6,896 crore. Operational data for Q2 FY27 (released October 1, 2026) showed generation up roughly 13% YoY, but full Q2 financial results are not yet out - management has previously reported in late October, so that release is the next thing to watch.
analysis.plain_terms: NTPC runs power plants and gets paid a regulated return, which is why its earnings are steadier than most companies. The tension here is that the stock is cheap on paper (P/E around 11x, well below Power Grid's ~15x and Tata Power's ~30x) but it is also sitting near a 52-week low, and its capital efficiency (ROCE ~8.9%) is modest for how much money is tied up in plants and debt. Cheap and unexciting are not the same as cheap and mispriced - this report tries to separate the two.
analysis.quarters: Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) standalone PAT jumped 34% YoY to ₹8,747 crore, but this was driven almost entirely by a one-off exceptional tax reversal of ₹9,062 crore (effective tax rate went negative), while revenue was roughly flat YoY - that PAT growth figure should not be read as operating improvement. Q1 FY27 looks cleaner: standalone PAT +11.9% YoY on revenue +3%, consolidated PAT +12.9% on revenue +7.8%, with EBITDA growth outpacing revenue. Management has reiterated FY27 capacity-addition guidance of 9.5 GW, including 8 GW of renewables, as the growth driver going forward. Full-year FY26 standalone PAT was ₹23,162 crore versus ₹19,649 crore in FY25, but that comparison is also inflated by the Q4 tax item - treat it as roughly high-teens underlying growth, not the ~18% headline implies at face value.
analysis.performance_read: There is no demerger or spin-off distorting NTPC's price history (the only corporate action on record is a 2019 bonus/split, already reflected in adjusted prices), so the 25.6% drawdown from the September 2024 peak is a genuine price fall, not a chart artifact. Zooming out, the stock has actually held up better than its sector and the market over the past year (-5.1% vs Nifty -9.8% and peer Tata Power -11.1%), and over three years is roughly in line with the peer (+39.1% vs +39.8%) while well ahead of the Nifty (+15.7%). The five-year return of 147.2% against the Nifty's 23.6% shows this was a strong compounder over the pandemic-recovery period - the recent pullback has come after that peak, not instead of long-term gains.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 11x and P/B of about 1.5x, NTPC is cheaper than both Power Grid (P/E ~14.9x, P/B ~2.3x) and Tata Power (P/E ~29.7x, P/B ~2.8x), and below the broader power-sector average of around 20x. Why it is cheap: NTPC's ROE (~14-15%) and especially ROCE (~8.9%) trail Power Grid's (ROE ~18.6%), reflecting that generation is more capital-intensive and lower-margin than Power Grid's asset-light transmission business, plus the market tends to discount state-owned utilities for lower perceived capital-allocation flexibility. Whether it is actually cheap is a separate question - on regulated, predictable cash flows the multiple looks undemanding, but the modest ROCE means the discount is at least partly earned, not purely sentiment.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin-led - revenue is growing in single digits (+3% to +8% YoY across recent quarters) as new capacity comes online, in line with a regulated cost-plus tariff model where margins don't expand much on their own. The real growth story is capacity: management's FY27 guidance of 9.5 GW of additions, including 8 GW of renewables through NTPC Green Energy, plus steady commissioning of smaller solar and wind projects (tens of MW at a time through mid-to-late 2026) rather than a single large profit lever.
analysis.health_read: NTPC's cash flows are backed by tripartite agreements that secure payment from state distribution companies, and both ICRA and CRISIL reaffirmed its AAA/Stable rating in 2026 - so business risk from the underlying operations is low. The watch item is financial risk from leverage: debt-to-equity runs around 1.1x (standalone) to 1.3x (consolidated), with total debt near ₹2.71 lakh crore funding the renewable capex buildout. Given the regulated revenue model and top-tier credit rating, this leverage looks manageable rather than alarming, but it is the thing to track as green-energy capex scales up.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Government of India, holding 51.1% as of June 2026, essentially unchanged quarter to quarter, with zero pledging - unsurprising for a sovereign-owned utility. Domestic institutions (DIIs) hold the largest non-promoter block at 29.4%, with FIIs at 16.3% (down slightly from 16.5% the prior quarter). No marquee individual investor shows up on the register in available data - if you were expecting to see a well-known name here, there isn't one.
strengths: AAA/Stable credit rating reaffirmed by both ICRA and CRISIL in 2026, reflecting secured cash flows under tripartite payment agreements
Consolidated Q1 FY27 PAT grew 12.9% YoY to ₹6,896 crore on revenue growth of 7.8%, a cleaner quarter than Q4 FY26's tax-boosted number
Zero promoter pledging against a stable 51.1% government holding
Five-year shareholder return of 147.2%, far ahead of the Nifty's 23.6% over the same stretch
watchpoints: Stock is trading essentially at its 52-week low (₹309.70), just ₹3.65 below the last close, and 25.6% below its September 2024 peak
ROCE of roughly 8.9% is modest for a capital-intensive generation business, raising the question of what returns the renewable capex buildout will actually generate
Q4 FY26's 34% PAT growth was driven by a one-off ₹9,062 crore exceptional tax reversal, not operations - don't extrapolate that growth rate forward
Total debt of roughly ₹2.71 lakh crore is funding an aggressive 9.5 GW FY27 capacity-addition target (8 GW of it renewables) - execution and funding cost are the swing factors
analysis.one_thing: The full Q2 FY27 financial results, expected late October or early November 2026, will show whether Q1's ~12-13% PAT growth holds up without a tax-related one-off, and whether the capacity additions are translating into proportionate earnings - that is what resolves whether the current cheap valuation is justified or overdone.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 results, credit ratings, and shareholding percentages are cross-checked across multiple sources (PSUConnect, ICICIDirect, Indian PSU, MarketsMojo, ICRA, CRISIL, Useflock/Trendlyne) but not verified directly against NTPC's own exchange filing PDFs, which were located but not fully extracted. Peer P/E, P/B and ROE figures for Tata Power and Power Grid are from aggregator data and should be checked on Screener before quoting precisely. Full Q2 FY27 financial results (only operational/generation data available as of this report) and the exact FY26 total dividend figure (minor discrepancy across sources around the ₹9.00/share total) are not independently verified - check NTPC's investor relations page or Screener before publishing exact figures.
